newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Hansa active on Estonian bourse, stability seen.
newsitem.headline: Hansa active on Estonian bourse, stability seen.

text.p: Hansapank was most traded stock on the Tallinn bourse on Monday and the market is expected to stay stable in May, dealers said.
Total trade was 47.1 million kroons versus 39.5 million kroons on Friday and the TALSE index gained 0.35 percent to close at 257.58.
"The market started modestly with minimum turnover, but ended with normal turnover," a dealer said.
"The market has won more reliability with buying interest emerging and with trade in large amounts," he added.
The market is expected to stay relatively stable during the following week unless some important news is announced, dealers said.
"An index change of plus 0.5-1 percent could be realistic," one dealer said.
Hansapank ended at 134.18 kroons versus 133.00 kroons in trade of 25.96 million kroons.
Farmaatsiatehas was the session's biggest gainer to close at 116 kroons vs 113 kroons on Friday. It turned over 1.4 million kroons.
Dealers said Farmaatsiateha's gain was prompted by its announcement on Friday that had it signed an agreement to establish a Russian factory and that it will raise its profit estimate for 1997.
Uhispank was the biggest loser on the main list to close at 51.35 kroons, against 52.75 kroons on Friday.
"Uhispank's price level in Helsinki is below its Tallinn level...and the share is more expensive compared to Hansapank and Forekspank," a dealer said.
Norma was the most active share on the free market in trade of 2.58 million kroons. It closed at 74 kroons, against 73.70 kroons on Friday.
Norma's activity was sparked by Friday's shareholders' meeting which approved all proposals and its April profit figures, dealers said.
